name: Spike - does a qualifying segment run with a short field
notes: Knockout qualifying writes each segment with only the cars still in it, so Q2 goes out as a five-car [CAR_n] list where Q1 was eight. Three things are being asked at once. First, does Content Manager accept and Assetto Corsa run a launch whose grid is smaller than the one before it - there is no reason it should not, a smaller grid is an ordinary thing, but nothing has ever changed the field size between launches of one weekend before. Second, do the result's car indices still mean positions in THAT launch's own [CAR_n] order - advanceWeekend maps them back through the order it launched with, and a segment that came back indexed against the full eight would put the wrong cars through. Third, does the composed grid come out right: the race should line up Q3's three, then Q2's two eliminated behind them, then Q1's three. PROCEDURE: run all four launches with npm run event -- spikes/knockout-qualifying, and SET A CLEAN FLYING LAP IN EVERY SEGMENT YOU ARE IN - a segment where you set nothing sorts you last and you go out, which is a valid run of the probe but tells you less. Between launches, read npm run event -- spikes/knockout-qualifying --status: it prints each segment's classification and, for one you were eliminated from, the order it invented instead. Note how many cars are on track in Q2 and Q3, and check cfg/race.ini straight after each launch for the [CAR_n] count. Then note the race grid before the lights and check it against the status output. Run it a second time after --reset while knocking yourself out in Q1 on purpose: Q2 and Q3 should be skipped and marked simulated, the race should still run, and you should line up exactly where Q1 left you.
